note: Research project “checkpoint recovery”. The agent is given: the user's paper PDFs + reading notes + experiment code documentation + experiment logs + Git commit notes + Word/PPT reports + meeting records for a certain research direction over the past year, where the project has been stalled for half a year. The user says: “I forgot where I got to with this idea. Help me restore this research project and tell me what is most worth continuing now.” The agent needs to: ① restore the research question as it was then; ② identify the validated/refuted hypotheses; ③ determine which results are credible based on the experiment records; ④ find the specific state of the last work; ⑤ identify the open questions that were not resolved at the time; ⑥ search the user's own notes to determine whether new ideas that appeared later can connect; ⑦ finally generate a “research state reconstruction” and give the next-step experiment plan. Difficulty: this is a very typical long-term memory + temporal reconstruction + research reasoning case, and “where I got to last” often does not exist in any single file.
env_description: research_archive/: notes/ (4 notes, including new notes from the stalled period that can connect to the original research), experiment_logs/ (4 logs, with planted experiment configuration changes that make results incomparable, and the blocker of the last experiment), git_log.txt (the WIP commit shows the last blocker was the DAG parser), 汇报/ (the final open questions), papers/README.md; the research question needs to be pieced together from multiple files.
